news.title: UEFA intensifies opposition to FIFA’s World Cup plans
news.lede: A week after the FIFA World Cup concluded with Spain lifting its second title, FIFA president Gianni Infantino proposed a new way of running international football. The idea, as he described it, was aimed at the “democratisation of football worldwide” while allowing private investors to take a stake in the global body’s competitions. UEFA, European football’s governing body, is set to hold an emergency meeting on Thursday (July 30, 2026) to discuss its response to the proposal. Here’s a look at what FIFA has proposed and how events could unfold in the coming weeks.

news.title: World Cup tourist confirms plans to return to the USA and follow another sport
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup brought thousands upon thousands of fans from many countries to North America. While the tournament ended on July 19 with Spain beating Argentina in the final, the impact on the USA appears to have been longer-lasting. Many tourists who visited America solely for the World Cup stayed long after their countries were knocked out of the competition, including viral fan Oliver Henry, who met President Donald Trump during his stint in the USA. Now, another soccer fan who became very popular during his time in America for the World Cup, ‘FreddyLA7’, has confirmed he’s set to travel back to the US later this year.

news.title: Emergency World Cup talks held today as Gianni Infantino plan rocks football
news.lede: European football will hold emergency talks today amid growing calls for a potential World Cup boycott after FIFA's controversial plans to sell a stake in its competitions sparked a major revolt. UEFA's 55 member associations are due to meet on Thursday to discuss a coordinated response after FIFA unveiled proposals to create FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a new company that would run the commercial side of its competitions. The plans would see FIFA sell a 20% stake in the company to outside investors, with the subsidiary carrying an estimated valuation of $20 billion (£15bn). news.lede: A strong English rejection of FIFA's proposal regarding the World Cup. Fury within European football over FIFA's proposal to restructure how it runs its tournaments, most notably the World Cup, shows no sign of fading. England fans have stepped up calls to boycott the competition just as the English Football Association leads moves within UEFA to confront a project raising widespread concerns about its future. news.title: Infantino defends plan to sell World Cup stakes but could Uefa launch boycott?
news.lede: Fifa President Gianni Infantino called the plan to sell stakes in the World Cup a proposal but “not an obligation” after the idea provoked a furious response from football authorities. Fifa announced plans this week to create a $20 billion subsidiary to run the World Cup and its other events, ⁠and said it will offer stakes of up to ​20 per cent ⁠in it to ‌external investors. The proposal drew strong criticism from the ​sport's regional confederations, who said they were blindsided by the plan from the world governing body. But Infantino said strengthening the commercial side of the game is the natural next step in this evolution.
